lines.text: Why do fingers wrinkle? It's your nerves, not only the water.
lines.phonemes: wˌaɪ dˈuː fˈɪŋɡəz ɹˈɪŋkəl? ɪts jɔː nˈɜːvz, nˌɒt ˈəʊnli ðə wˈɔːtə.

lines.text: After about fifteen minutes in water, the hairless skin on your hands and feet has folded deeply. It is an active process, run by your nervous system.
lines.phonemes: ˈaftəɹ ɐbˌaʊt fˈɪftiːn mˈɪnɪts ɪn wˈɔːtə, ðə hˈeələs skˈɪn ˌɒn jɔː hˈandz and fˈiːt hɐz fˈəʊldɪd dˈiːpli. ɪt ɪz ɐn ˈaktɪv pɹˈəʊsɛs, ɹˈʌn baɪ jɔː nˈɜːvəs sˈɪstəm.

lines.text: When nerves tell the tiny blood vessels in your fingertips to narrow, the tissue below shrinks a little. Scientists think the skin above then folds into ridges.
lines.phonemes: wˌɛn nˈɜːvz tˈɛl ðə tˈaɪni blˈʌd vˈɛsəlz ɪn jɔː fˈɪŋɡətˌɪps tə nˈaɹəʊ, ðə tˈɪʃuː bɪlˌəʊ ʃɹˈɪŋks ɐ lˈɪtəl. sˈaɪəntɪsts θˈɪŋk ðə skˈɪn əbˌʌv ðˈɛn fˈəʊldz ˌɪntʊ ɹˈɪdʒɪz.

lines.text: Doctors have used this to test nerves for over eighty years. When the nerves to a finger stop working, the finger does not wrinkle. So the wrinkles are a sign of working nerves, not just soaking.
lines.phonemes: dˈɒktəz hav jˈuːzd ðɪs tə tˈɛst nˈɜːvz fɔːɹ ˌəʊvəɹ ˈeɪti jˈiəz. wˌɛn ðə nˈɜːvz tʊ ɐ fˈɪŋɡə stˈɒp wˈɜːkɪŋ, ðə fˈɪŋɡə dʌznˌɒt ɹˈɪŋkəl. sˌəʊ ðə ɹˈɪŋkəlz ɑːɹ ɐ sˈaɪn ɒv wˈɜːkɪŋ nˈɜːvz, nˌɒt dʒˈʌst sˈəʊkɪŋ.

lines.text: Why would the body do this? One idea is grip. In one study, people handled wet objects faster with wrinkled fingers. A later study found no difference.
lines.phonemes: wˌaɪ wʊd ðə bˈɒdi dˈuː ðˈɪs? wˈɒn aɪdˈiəɹ ɪz ɡɹˈɪp. ɪn wˈɒn stˈʌdi, pˈiːpəl hˈandəld wˈɛt ˈɒbdʒɛkts fˈastə wɪð ɹˈɪŋkəld fˈɪŋɡəz. ɐ lˈeɪtə stˈʌdi fˈaʊnd nˈəʊ dˈɪfɹəns.

lines.text: Quick thing: like and follow. Your skin has plenty more secrets.
lines.phonemes: kwˈɪk θˈɪŋ: lˈaɪk and fˈɒləʊ. jɔː skˈɪn hɐz plˈɛnti mˈɔː sˈiːkɹɪts.

lines.text: So wrinkled fingers are your nerves at work. Whether they help you grip is still debated.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ ɹˈɪŋkəld fˈɪŋɡəz ɑː jɔː nˈɜːvz at wˈɜːk. wˈɛðə ðeɪ hˈɛlp juː ɡɹˈɪp ɪz stˈɪl dɪbˈeɪtɪd.

lines.text: Next: how sweat really cools you. Cooling happens when sweat dries.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: hˌaʊ swˈɛt ɹˈiəlɪ kˈuːlz juː. kˈuːlɪŋ hˈapənz wɛn swˈɛt dɹˈaɪz.
